message.content:
Below is a concise summary of your key rights and protections as a residential tenant in Texas (as of 2024). These apply to most private rental agreements—though some rules may differ for public housing, student dorms, or other special arrangements. | Area | What You’re Entitled To | How It’s Enforced | |------|------------------------|-------------------| | **Security Deposit** | • Must be no more than one month’s rent (or two if you’re renting a furnished unit).
• Landlord must return it within 30 days after you move out, minus any lawful deductions. | • Texas Property Code §92.001–92.004 governs deposits. | | **Habitability & Repairs** | • Landlord must keep the premises safe, sanitary, and in good repair.
• Must fix major problems (plumbing, heating, structural issues) promptly. | • If repairs aren’t made, you can withhold rent, pay yourself, or break the lease (see §92.006). | | **Notice Requirements** | • For non‑payment of rent: 3‑day written notice before eviction.
• For lease termination: 30‑day notice for month‑to‑month; 60‑days for longer leases. | • Notices must be in writing and delivered personally or via certified mail. | | **Eviction Process** | • Landlord must file an unlawful detainer action in court.
• Court will issue a summons and order a hearing.
• You have the right to contest and present evidence. | • Texas Courts handle all eviction proceedings; you can request a stay if you’re facing hardship. | | **Right to Privacy** | • Landlord may enter only for emergencies, repairs, inspections, or to show the unit, with reasonable notice (usually 24 hrs). | • Unreasonable entry can be grounds for a complaint or lawsuit. | | **Discrimination Protections** | • Protected against discrimination based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, familial status, or source of income (e.g., public assistance). | • File complaints with the Texas Attorney General or HUD. | | **Lease Terms** | • Lease must be in writing if it lasts longer than one year.
• Landlord cannot add illegal clauses (e.g., waiving your right to a habitable home). | • Courts can invalidate unfair or illegal terms. | | **Rent Increases** | • No statutory limit on how much a landlord can raise rent, but they must give proper notice (typically 30 days for month‑to‑month). | • Some cities have local rent‑control ordinances; check your municipality. | | **Utilities** | • Landlord must provide essential services (heat, hot water, electricity, gas).
• If utilities are separate, you must pay them directly. | • Failure to maintain utilities can be a breach of the lease. | | **Subletting & Assignment** | • Generally allowed unless prohibited by lease; you must get written permission. | • Unauthorized subletting can lead to lease termination. | | **Legal Remedies** | • Withhold rent, repair & deduct, break lease, sue for damages, or seek mediation. | • Texas courts and local housing agencies can help enforce rights. | ### Quick Steps If You Face Problems 1. **Document Everything** – Keep copies of notices, emails, photos of damage, and receipts for repairs or withheld rent. 2. **Communicate in Writing** – Send all correspondence via certified mail or email with read receipts. 3. **Know Your Timeline** – Pay attention to the 3‑day notice for non‑payment and the 30‑/60‑day notice for lease termination. 4. **Seek Mediation** – Many counties offer free or low‑cost mediation services for landlord‑tenant disputes. 5. **File a Complaint** – If you suspect discrimination or illegal practices, contact the Texas Attorney General’s Office or HUD. 6. **Consult an Attorney** – For complex cases (e.g., eviction, large deposit disputes), consider hiring a lawyer who specializes in landlord‑tenant law. --- #### Useful Resources | Resource | What It Offers | Link | |----------|---------------|------| | Texas Attorney General – Housing Division | Discrimination complaints, consumer protection, legal guidance | https://www.texasattorneygeneral.gov/housing | | Texas Department of Housing and Community Affairs | Fair housing enforcement, HUD compliance | https://www.tdhca.state.tx.us | | Local County Clerk’s Office | Eviction filings, court orders | Search online for your county clerk | | Texas Legal Services | Free legal advice for low‑income residents | https://www.texaslegalservices.org | | HUD’s Fair Housing Hotline | 24‑hour hotline for discrimination questions | https://www.hud.gov | Feel free to ask if you need more detail on any particular point, or if you'd like help drafting a notice or understanding a specific clause in your lease!
